          "edits": [
            [
              {
                "text": "# Parking Garage Attendant System\n\nA complete FastAPI web application and CLI for a configurable parking garage\nwith tiered fees, EV-only charging spots, compact/standard overflow, and\nconstant-time-style live lookups.\n\n## Features\n\n- Live check-in, check-out, plate lookup, availability, and transaction history.\n- Indian registration plate validation and canonical formatting.\n- Separate attendant and customer portals with mock-payment reservations.\n- Staff signup/login uses PBKDF2 password hashes and signed HTTP-only session cookies. Customer reservations remain guest-accessible.\n- Seven-second polling keeps both portals current without a manual refresh.\n- Responsive dashboard served by FastAPI with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.\n- Atomic in-memory spot assignment protected for concurrent requests.\n- Configurable levels, spot counts, rates, and per-stay daily cap.\n\n## Policies\n\n- Partial hours round up: a stay of 1 hour and 1 minute is charged as 2 hours.\n- The first charged hour uses `first_hour_rate`; every later charged hour uses\n\t`additional_hour_rate`.\n- Fees are displayed in Indian Rupees (`₹`); fee amounts remain numeric\n\tinternally.\n- `daily_cap` is a per-stay maximum. It applies to the elapsed stay from entry\n\tto exit and is not tied to the calendar date.\n- Compact vehicles prefer compact spots and overflow into standard spots when\n\tneeded. Standard vehicles do the reverse. Neither type can use EV spots.\n- EV vehicles may use only EV spots.\n- Plates accept `KA01AB1234` or `MH-12-CD-5678` style input: two state letters,\n  two RTO digits, one or two series letters, and four digits. Input is\n  uppercased and stored canonically as `STATE-RTO-SERIES-NUMBER`, for example\n  `KA-01-AB-1234`.\n\n## Reservations and customer portal\n\nOpen `/customer` for the customer-only portal. It shows live availability, the\n₹ rate card, a near-term arrival-window form, mock payment, and reservation\nlookup/cancellation. The attendant dashboard remains at `/` and shows paid\nupcoming reservations with a check-in conversion action.\n\n- A reservation is limited to the next 24 hours and has a specific arrival\n\twindow.\n- A pending reservation does not remove a spot from availability. It has 10\n\tminutes to complete mock payment.\n- After payment, one compatible spot is held until the arrival window ends.\n- Expired or cancelled reservations release their held spot immediately.\n- A plate may have only one active pending or paid reservation.\n- Confirmation codes are six uppercase letters/digits, such as `PK4X9B`.\n- Late arrivals are treated as normal walk-ins after the reservation expires.\n- No real payment provider is used; mock payment only changes reservation state.\n- UPI reservations require the explicit mock UPI step before a spot is held.\n- Cash reservations hold the spot immediately and remain `payment_status: pending`\n\tuntil the attendant collects cash at the gate.\n\nThe portals use short-interval polling every seven seconds because it is a\nsmall, reliable addition to the existing FastAPI app and avoids introducing a\nWebSocket connection manager for this in-memory version.\n\nWhen the shared `/clock` sweep runs, paid or cash-pending reservations whose\narrival window ended more than 30 minutes ago are auto-cancelled as no-shows\nand their held spots are released. A reservation checked in before that grace\nperiod is never cancelled by the sweep.\n\n## Nightly auto-close and test clock\n\n`POST /clock` is a test hook that stands in for a real nightly cron job. Send\neither `{\"set_time\":\"2026-09-18T14:00:00\"}` or\n`{\"advance_hours\":25}`. The endpoint updates the shared injectable clock and\nimmediately sweeps active sessions.\n\nAny session parked for more than 24 hours is force-closed. Auto-close billing\nuses rolling 24-hour periods from entry, with one configured daily cap per\nperiod: a 30-hour stay is billed as 2 daily caps. The spot is freed, the ticket\nis added to history with `auto_closed: true`, and a later sweep cannot process\nit again. Normal checkout uses the same clock source and lock.\n\n## Valet transfer\n\n`POST /transfer` accepts `{\"old_plate\":\"KA01AB1234\",\"new_plate\":\"MH12CD5678\"}`.\nIt changes the active ticket's plate while preserving its spot and entry time.\nThe transfer is atomic, never releases the spot, and rejects a missing source\nor an already-active destination plate.\n\n## Rate-card import status\n\nThe requested dirty rate-card payload was not included in the supplied\nspecification; it still contains the literal placeholder\n`<PASTE YOUR MESSY RATE CARD DATA HERE>`. The current configured rates remain\nthe existing sample values until the real payload is provided. No rates were\ninvented during this change, because doing so would silently change billing.\n\n## Run tests\n\n```bash\npython3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt\npython3 -m pytest -v\n```\n\n## Run the web application\n\n```bash\nuvicorn src.api:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000\n```\n\nIn GitHub Codespaces, open the forwarded port `8000` in the Ports panel. The\nroot page is the attendant dashboard.\n\nYou can also run `python3 run.py`.\n\n## API\n\n- `POST /api/check-in` with `{\"plate\":\"KA01AB1234\",\"vehicle_type\":\"ev\"}`\n- `POST /api/check-out` with `{\"plate\":\"KA-01-AB-1234\"}`\n- `GET /api/vehicle/{plate}`\n- `GET /api/spots/availability`\n- `GET /api/spots/availability/{spot_type}`\n- `GET /api/transactions`\n- `GET /api/dashboard`\n- `GET /customer`\n- `GET /api/customer/config`\n- `POST /api/reservations`\n- `POST /api/reservations/{code}/pay`\n- `GET /api/reservations/lookup?plate=...` or `?code=...`\n- `POST /api/reservations/{code}/cancel`\n- `POST /api/reservations/{code}/check-in`\n- `GET /api/reservations`\n- `POST /clock`\n- `POST /transfer`\n\nThe API returns `409` for duplicate check-ins and unavailable compatible spots,\n`404` for missing active vehicles, and `422` for invalid request data.\n\n## Architecture\n\n`models.py`, `rate_card.py`, and `garage.py` contain framework-independent\nbusiness logic. `api.py` adapts those objects to HTTP. The browser dashboard\nuses `fetch()` and updates only affected regions after each action. Active\nvehicles use `dict[plate, Ticket]`; free spots use\n`dict[SpotType, set[spot_id]]`; completed transactions stay in a separate\nappend-only list. These live operations do not scan transaction history.\n\n## Run the CLI\n\n```bash\npython -m src.cli\n```\n\nThe default CLI configuration is only an example. `ParkingGarage` accepts the\nnumber of levels, spots per level by type, and a `RateCard`, so applications can\nprovide any garage configuration.\n\n## Design\n\nCurrently parked vehicles are stored in `active_tickets`, indexed by plate.\nFree spots are indexed by `SpotType` and spot ID. Completed tickets are appended\nto the separate `history` list, so historical log growth does not require scans\nfor check-in, checkout, plate lookup, or availability queries.\n\n## Stretch features\n\n1. Persist completed transactions and restore active state after a restart.\n2. Add reservations and a queue for full spot types.\n3. Add daily reports for revenue, occupancy, and average stay duration.",

                  "arguments": "{\"input\":\"*** Begin Patch\\n*** Update File: /workspaces/Parking_Garage/README.md\\n@@\\n - Separate attendant and customer portals with mock-payment reservations.\\n+- Staff signup/login uses PBKDF2 password hashes and signed HTTP-only session cookies.         {
          "value": "Implemented and validated the requested updates.\n\n### Authentication\n\n- Added staff signup, login, logout, and session cookies.\n- Passwords are hashed with PBKDF2-HMAC.\n- Added `/login`.\n- Attendant page redirects to login once staff accounts exist.\n- Logged-in staff name/email populate the sidebar.\n- Customer portal remains guest-accessible.\n- Added visible logout control.\n\n### Payment Flow\n\n- Added explicit UPI vs Cash selection.\n- UPI requires a mock UPI ID.\n- Cash reservations hold the spot immediately.\n- Cash reservations remain `payment_status: pending`.\n- Added cash collection API support.\n- Reservation confirmations expose:\n  - Payment method\n  - Payment status\n  - Payment amount\n  - Confirmation code\n  - Arrival window\n  - Cancellation action\n\n### No-Show Rule\n\nIntegrated into the existing `/clock` sweep:\n\n- Arrival window ended 20 minutes ago: reservation remains held.\n- Arrival window ended over 30 minutes ago: reservation auto-expires and releases its spot.\n- Checked-in reservations are never cancelled by the no-show sweep.\n\n### UX Refresh\n\n- Added animated stat transitions.\n- Added card entrance motion and hover elevation.\n- Added live staff identity display.\n- Added logout control.\n- Improved customer payment clarity.\n- Added explicit cash/UPI messaging.\n- Preserved responsive layouts and existing portal structure.\n\n### Validation\n\nBaseline before changes:\n\n```text\n34 passed\n```\n\nFinal suite:\n\n```text\n38 passed, 1 warning\n```\n\nThe warning is the existing Starlette/httpx deprecation warning.\n\nLive verification passed:\n\n```text\ncustomer=200\nlogin=200\nstaff signup/session succeeded\nreservation API succeeded\n```\n\nThe app is running on port `8000`.\n\nNote: existing operational API routes remain backward-compatible for the current test and integration contract; the attendant page itself is session-gated once staff accounts exist.",

            {
              "response": "Implemented and validated the requested updates.\n\n### Authentication\n\n- Added staff signup, login, logout, and session cookies.\n- Passwords are hashed with PBKDF2-HMAC.\n- Added `/login`.\n- Attendant page redirects to login once staff accounts exist.\n- Logged-in staff name/email populate the sidebar.\n- Customer portal remains guest-accessible.\n- Added visible logout control.\n\n### Payment Flow\n\n- Added explicit UPI vs Cash selection.\n- UPI requires a mock UPI ID.\n- Cash reservations hold the spot immediately.\n- Cash reservations remain `payment_status: pending`.\n- Added cash collection API support.\n- Reservation confirmations expose:\n  - Payment method\n  - Payment status\n  - Payment amount\n  - Confirmation code\n  - Arrival window\n  - Cancellation action\n\n### No-Show Rule\n\nIntegrated into the existing `/clock` sweep:\n\n- Arrival window ended 20 minutes ago: reservation remains held.\n- Arrival window ended over 30 minutes ago: reservation auto-expires and releases its spot.\n- Checked-in reservations are never cancelled by the no-show sweep.\n\n### UX Refresh\n\n- Added animated stat transitions.\n- Added card entrance motion and hover elevation.\n- Added live staff identity display.\n- Added logout control.\n- Improved customer payment clarity.\n- Added explicit cash/UPI messaging.\n- Preserved responsive layouts and existing portal structure.\n\n### Validation\n\nBaseline before changes:\n\n```text\n34 passed\n```\n\nFinal suite:\n\n```text\n38 passed, 1 warning\n```\n\nThe warning is the existing Starlette/httpx deprecation warning.\n\nLive verification passed:\n\n```text\ncustomer=200\nlogin=200\nstaff signup/session succeeded\nreservation API succeeded\n```\n\nThe app is running on port `8000`.\n\nNote: existing operational API routes remain backward-compatible for the current test and integration contract; the attendant page itself is session-gated once staff accounts exist.",

                "text": "# Parking Garage Attendant System\n\nA FastAPI parking garage application with two browser portals and a small\nPython CLI:\n\n- `/`: attendant control room for check-in, checkout, search, reports, and\n  upcoming reservations.\n- `/customer`: guest customer portal for live availability, rate transparency,\n  near-term reservations, mock payment, lookup, and cancellation.\n\nThe core parking logic is framework-independent Python. The current application\nuses in-memory state; restarting the process resets active cars, reservations,\nstaff users, sessions, and transaction history.\n\n## Features and policies\n\n- Configurable levels, spot counts, and rates through `ParkingGarage`.\n- Compact vehicles prefer compact spots and overflow into standard spots.\n- Standard vehicles prefer standard spots and overflow into compact spots.\n- Neither compact nor standard vehicles can use EV spots.\n- EV vehicles can use only EV spots.\n- Free spots are indexed by `SpotType`; active cars are indexed by canonical\n  plate.\n- Indian plates accept formats such as `KA01AB1234` and `MH-12-CD-5678`.\n  They are uppercased and stored as `KA-01-AB-1234`.\n- Fees are displayed in Indian Rupees (`₹`). Values remain numeric `Decimal`\n  values internally.\n- Partial hours always round up. A zero-duration or one-minute stay charges at\n  least the first-hour rate.\n- The normal `RateCard` daily cap limits one continuous parking stay.\n- The `/clock` auto-close sweep force-closes active stays over 24 hours. Its\n  billing uses rolling 24-hour periods from entry: a 30-hour stay is billed as\n  two daily caps, and a 49-hour stay as three daily caps.\n\n## Setup in Codespaces\n\nFrom the repository root:\n\n```bash\npython3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt\npython3 -m pytest -v\npython3 -m uvicorn src.api:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000\n```\n\nThe alternative launcher is:\n\n```bash\npython3 run.py\n```\n\nOpen port `8000` in the VS Code Codespaces **Ports** panel. The URLs are:\n\n- Attendant portal: `http://localhost:8000/`\n- Staff login: `http://localhost:8000/login`\n- Customer portal: `http://localhost:8000/customer`\n\nThe browser portals poll the backend every seven seconds instead of using\nWebSockets. This is intentionally simple for the in-memory FastAPI deployment.\n\n## Configuration\n\nThere are currently no required environment variables. The default application\nconfiguration is defined in `src/api.py`:\n\n- 3 levels\n- 10 compact spots per level\n- 15 standard spots per level\n- 5 EV spots per level\n- first hour: `50`\n- additional hour: `30`\n- daily cap: `200`\n\n`src/auth.py` currently uses an in-memory `AuthStore` and a development fallback\nsigning secret. The secret is not read from an environment variable yet. Do not\nuse this authentication setup as production security without moving users,\nsessions, and the signing secret to durable, environment-based configuration.\n\n## Portals\n\n### Attendant portal\n\nThe attendant dashboard provides check-in, checkout, plate lookup, availability,\nreports, transaction history, an upcoming-reservation queue, and conversion of a\npaid reservation into an active check-in. It also exposes the staff identity in\nthe sidebar after login.\n\nStaff can create an account and sign in at `/login`. Passwords are stored as\nPBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hashes. Successful signup/login sets an HTTP-only,\nSameSite cookie named `staff_session`.\n\n### Customer portal\n\nThe customer portal is intentionally guest-first. Customers do not need an\naccount to reserve, pay, find, or cancel a reservation. The current UI supports:\n\n- live compact, standard, and EV availability;\n- the current ₹ rate card;\n- Indian plate input and a same-day/near-term arrival window;\n- explicit UPI or cash-at-gate selection;\n- mock UPI ID validation and confirmation;\n- reservation confirmation details immediately after payment/confirmation;\n- lookup by plate or six-character confirmation code;\n- cancellation before check-in.\n\nCustomer email accounts are not implemented. This keeps one-time parking\nlow-friction, as requested.\n\n## Reservation rules\n\n- Confirmation codes are six uppercase letters/digits.\n- A plate can have at most one active pending or paid reservation.\n- Reservations are limited to the next 24 hours.\n- A pending UPI reservation does not consume a free spot. The payment window is\n  10 minutes.\n- UPI payment holds a compatible spot only after the mock payment succeeds.\n- Cash confirmation holds a compatible spot and reports `payment_status: pending`;\n  cash collection is represented by `POST /api/reservations/{code}/cash-collected`.\n- Paid/cash-held reservations release their spot on cancellation or expiration.\n- `POST /clock` applies the no-show rule as part of the same sweep as active-car\n  auto-close: a reservation whose arrival window ended more than 30 minutes ago\n  is expired and its held spot is released. A checked-in reservation is not\n  cancelled by this sweep.\n\nThe current code also invokes reservation expiry during some ordinary garage\noperations. For exact grace-period testing, use `/clock`, which is the intended\nnightly sweep hook and is covered by the tests.\n\n## API reference\n\n### Pages and static assets\n\n- `GET /` - attendant dashboard; redirects to `/login` after at least one staff\n  account exists and the request has no valid staff cookie.\n- `GET /login` - staff login page.\n- `GET /customer` - customer portal; no staff authentication required.\n- `GET /static/{asset_path}` - CSS and JavaScript assets.\n\n### Authentication\n\n- `POST /api/auth/signup`\n  - body: `{\"name\":\"Asha Rao\",\"email\":\"asha@example.com\",\"password\":\"securepass\"}`\n- `POST /api/auth/login`\n  - body: `{\"email\":\"asha@example.com\",\"password\":\"securepass\"}`\n- `POST /api/auth/logout`\n- `GET /api/auth/me`\n\n### Live garage operations\n\n- `POST /api/check-in`\n  - body: `{\"plate\":\"KA01AB1234\",\"vehicle_type\":\"ev\"}`\n- `POST /api/check-out`\n  - body: `{\"plate\":\"KA-01-AB-1234\"}`\n- `GET /api/vehicle/{plate}`\n- `GET /api/spots/availability`\n- `GET /api/spots/availability/{compact|standard|ev}`\n- `GET /api/transactions`\n  - optional `plate`, `from_date`, `to_date`, `page`, and `page_size` query\n    parameters.\n- `GET /api/dashboard`\n- `GET /api/reports`\n\n### Customer and reservations\n\n- `GET /api/customer/config` - current rate card and 10-minute payment window.\n- `POST /api/reservations`\n  - body includes `plate`, `vehicle_type`, `arrival_start`, `arrival_end`, and\n    optional `payment_method` (`upi` or `cash`).\n- `POST /api/reservations/{code}/pay`\n  - optional body: `{\"payment_method\":\"upi\",\"upi_id\":\"name@bank\"}`.\n  - A no-body request remains supported for backward compatibility in the\n    current test suite.\n- `GET /api/reservations/lookup?plate=...` or `?code=...`\n- `POST /api/reservations/{code}/cancel`\n- `POST /api/reservations/{code}/check-in`\n- `POST /api/reservations/{code}/cash-collected`\n- `GET /api/reservations`\n\n### Maintenance and valet operations\n\n- `POST /clock`\n  - body is exactly one of `{\"set_time\":\"2026-09-18T14:00:00\"}` or\n    `{\"advance_hours\":25}`.\n  - Returns the updated time and tickets auto-closed in that sweep.\n- `POST /transfer`\n  - body: `{\"old_plate\":\"KA01AB1234\",\"new_plate\":\"MH12CD5678\"}`.\n  - Keeps the same spot and entry time without releasing the spot.\n\n## Errors and debugging\n\nCommon status codes:\n\n- `400`: invalid plate, invalid time/rate input, or another expected domain\n  validation error.\n- `401`: invalid staff credentials or unauthenticated `/api/auth/me`.\n- `404`: missing active vehicle or reservation.\n- `409`: duplicate active plate, no compatible spot, duplicate reservation,\n  conflicting reservation state, or occupied transfer destination.\n- `422`: malformed request validation, invalid clock command, or malformed\n  lookup/filter input.\n\nUseful commands:\n\n```bash\n# Run everything\npython3 -m pytest -v\n\n# Run one layer\npython3 -m pytest tests/test_rate_card.py -q\npython3 -m pytest tests/test_garage.py -q\npython3 -m pytest tests/test_api.py -q\n\n# Check syntax\npython3 -m compileall -q src tests\n```\n\nTo reset all in-memory state, stop and restart Uvicorn. That clears the garage,\nreservations, staff users, sessions, clock, and history. Tests isolate their\n`ParkingGarage` instances and monkeypatch the API garage fixture.\n\nIf `/` redirects unexpectedly, sign up or log in at `/login`. If a plate is\nrejected, use two state letters, two RTO digits, one or two series letters, and\nfour digits, with optional hyphens. If a payment hold is unavailable, check\n`/api/spots/availability` and the reservation status returned by the API.\n\n## CLI\n\nThe alternate CLI remains in `src/cli.py`:\n\n```bash\npython3 -m src.cli\n```\n\nIt supports check-in, checkout, availability, active-car lookup, and exit. It is\nseparate from both browser portals and is retained as a useful development and\noperations interface.\n\n## Rate-card import status\n\nNo messy rate-card payload was present in the project or supplied specification;\nthe earlier placeholder was literally `<PASTE YOUR MESSY RATE CARD DATA HERE>`.\nTherefore no T4 cleaning module was invented and no production rates were\nsilently changed. The active app still constructs `RateCard(50, 30, 200)` in\n`build_garage()`. A real importer should be added only after the actual source\npayload is supplied.\n\n## Known limitations and next steps\n\n- State is process-local and disappears on restart; add a database and durable\n  migrations for production.\n- Staff users and sessions are in memory; move them to durable storage and read\n  the signing secret from an environment variable.\n- Most operational API routes remain callable without a staff cookie for\n  backward compatibility; only the attendant HTML root is redirect-gated when\n  accounts exist.\n- Mock UPI and cash collection have no real payment provider or audit ledger.\n- The CLI does not include reservations or staff authentication.\n- Polling is used instead of WebSockets.\n- The rate-card importer is still pending the real dirty input data.\n- Add persistent reservations, role-based staff permissions, CSRF protection,\n  rate-card versioning, and structured audit logging next.\n",

                  "endLineNumber": 1,
                  "endColumn": 1
                }

                "text": "# Implementation Reasoning\n\nThis document describes the system that is actually in the repository, not an\nintended future architecture.\n\n## Core design\n\n### `Vehicle`\n\n`Vehicle` owns the license plate and `SpotType`. Construction calls\n`normalize_plate`, so all domain objects use one canonical Indian plate form:\n`STATE-RTO-SERIES-NUMBER`, such as `KA-01-AB-1234`.\n\n### `Spot`\n\n`Spot` represents one physical location with a level, spot type, charger flag,\nand occupancy metadata. EV spots are created with `has_charger=True`. The\n`reservation_code`, `vehicle`, and `ticket_id` references make the current\nphysical state visible without searching history.\n\n### `Ticket`\n\n`Ticket` is the live or completed parking session. It records the vehicle,\nspot, entry/exit timestamps, fee, generated ticket ID, and whether the session\nwas force-closed by the 24-hour sweep.\n\n### `RateCard`\n\n`RateCard` is isolated from garage allocation. It accepts already-clean numeric\nrates and calculates a per-stay fee using `Decimal`. It rounds a partial hour\nup and charges at least one first-hour rate, including for an immediate\ncheckout. Normal fees are capped by `daily_cap`.\n\n### `Clock`\n\n`Clock` is a small thread-safe injectable time source. It defaults to\n`datetime.now()` but supports `set_time` and `advance_hours`, allowing tests\nand `POST /clock` to exercise time-dependent behavior without waiting.\n\n### `Reservation`\n\n`Reservation` records a six-character confirmation code, canonical plate,\nvehicle type, arrival window, payment deadline, status, held spot, payment\nmethod, payment status, and displayed payment amount. `PaymentMethod` supports\nUPI and cash; `PaymentStatus` distinguishes pending, paid, and collected.\n\n### `ParkingGarage`\n\n`ParkingGarage` owns spot construction and the state transitions for check-in,\ncheckout, reservations, auto-close, and transfer. A single `Lock` protects\nallocation, releases, reservations, transfer, and history mutations.\n\n## O(1)-style live lookups\n\nThe garage deliberately separates live state from completed history:\n\n- `active_tickets: dict[str, Ticket]` maps canonical plate to the current car.\n- `free_spots: dict[SpotType, set[str]]` tracks available physical spot IDs.\n- `spots: dict[str, Spot]` resolves a spot ID to its level and state.\n- `reservations: dict[str, Reservation]` indexes confirmation codes.\n- `reservation_by_plate: dict[str, str]` enforces one active reservation per\n  plate and supports plate lookup without scanning the log.\n- `history: list[Ticket]` is append-only completed transaction history.\n\nCheck-in pops from a compatible free set; checkout returns the spot to that\nset. Plate lookup, free-spot checks, and active-state checks do not scan\n`history`, so historical growth does not make those operations linear in the\nday's transaction count. Reservation lookup by plate is an index lookup; the\nhistory list is not involved.\n\n## T4 messy rate-card import\n\nT4 is not implemented. The supplied material contained the literal placeholder\n`<PASTE YOUR MESSY RATE CARD DATA HERE>`, not actual rows. Consequently:\n\n- there is no `clean_rate_card` importer module;\n- no duplicate-row or missing-field tie-break rule was applied;\n- no broken-row behavior can honestly be documented;\n- `build_garage()` still constructs `RateCard(50, 30, 200)`.\n\nInventing a cleaning rule or rates without source data would silently alter\nbilling. The correct next step is to add a separate parser with explicit tests\nonce the real payload is available. `RateCard` already receives clean values\nand remains independent of parsing.\n\n## T2 rolling-24-hour billing and `/clock`\n\n`ParkingGarage.auto_close_overdue()` runs under the same lock as normal\ncheckout. It scans active tickets only, identifies sessions strictly over 24\nhours, removes them from `active_tickets`, computes:\n\n```text\nceil((clock_time - entry_time) / 24 hours) * daily_cap\n```\n\nand releases the spot. The ticket is appended to history with\n`auto_closed=True`. A normal checkout removes the ticket first, so a later\nsweep cannot process it twice.\n\n`POST /clock` updates the shared `Clock`, runs the reservation no-show sweep,\nthen runs active-session auto-close, and returns the auto-closed tickets. It is\nthe test hook standing in for a nightly cron job.\n\nThe clock endpoint accepts either `set_time` or `advance_hours`, but not both.\nThe default garage and API clock are process-local, so restarting the server\nresets the simulated time and all other state.\n\n## T6 valet transfer\n\n`ParkingGarage.transfer(old_plate, new_plate)` normalizes both plates and runs\nunder the garage lock. It verifies that the old plate is active and the new\nplate is not. It then changes the ticket's plate and vehicle reference and\nupdates the occupied spot's vehicle reference. It never removes or re-adds the\nspot in `free_spots`, so availability cannot flicker to free during transfer.\nEntry time, spot ID, ticket ID, and subsequent fee calculation remain intact.\nThe API maps missing sessions to 404 and an occupied destination to 409.\n\n## Reservation holds and no-show behavior\n\nThe intended reservation lifecycle is:\n\n1. Create a near-term reservation. A normal UPI reservation starts as\n   `pending_payment` and does not remove a spot from `free_spots`.\n2. Confirm UPI payment. The backend atomically pops a compatible spot and marks\n   the reservation paid.\n3. Confirm cash-at-gate. The current payment endpoint can switch the\n   reservation to cash and hold a compatible spot immediately; its payment\n   status remains pending until the cash-collection endpoint is called.\n4. Cancel, check in, or expire the reservation. Cancellation and expiration\n   release a held spot; conversion changes the reserved spot into an occupied\n   active ticket.\n\nThe shared `/clock` sweep applies the 30-minute no-show grace rule to paid\nreservations: after an arrival window has ended by more than 30 minutes, the\nreservation is expired and its held spot is released. Checked-in reservations\nhave status `checked_in` and are not touched. Keeping this in the same sweep\nas T2 ensures one simulated nightly event updates both overdue cars and\nno-show reservations atomically under the garage lock.\n\nImportant current-state detail: ordinary reservation reads and some garage\noperations call the general expiry helper without the grace flag, while\n`auto_close_overdue()` calls it with `apply_no_show_grace=True`. The documented\nand tested grace-period mechanism is therefore specifically the `/clock`\nsweep; this is an area to simplify if the expiry semantics are hardened later.\n\n## Authentication design\n\n`AuthStore` is an in-memory staff identity/session service:\n\n- staff signup accepts name, email, and an eight-character minimum password;\n- passwords are PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hashes with per-user salts;\n- login issues a signed, HTTP-only, SameSite cookie;\n- logout removes the server-side session mapping;\n- the attendant root redirects to `/login` after at least one account exists;\n- `/api/auth/me` supplies the sidebar identity.\n\nCustomers deliberately remain guest users. A plate plus confirmation code is\nsufficient for reservation lookup/cancellation, which avoids account friction\nfor a one-time parking visit. Optional customer email accounts are not built.\n\nThis is suitable for a demonstrator, not production authentication. The store\nand sessions are process-local, the fallback signing secret is in code, and\nmost operational API routes are not protected by an auth dependency yet. A\nproduction version should use a database, an environment secret, expiration,\nCSRF protection, and route-level authorization.\n\n## Known limitations and next steps\n\n- T4 rate-card import is blocked on missing source data.\n- No persistent database exists.\n- No real UPI gateway or payment ledger exists.\n- Cash collection is a state transition, not a financial reconciliation flow.\n- Polling is used instead of WebSockets.\n- The CLI supports core parking operations but not reservations or auth.\n- Reports use process-local history and `datetime.now()` rather than a durable\n  reporting clock.\n- Add durable storage, migrations, role-based staff permissions, route-level\n  auth dependencies, environment configuration, structured audit events, and\n  integration/browser tests next.\n",

                  "endColumn": 1
                }

                  "arguments": "{\"filePath\":\"/workspaces/Parking_Garage/README.md\",\"content\":\"# Parking Garage Attendant System\\n\\nA FastAPI parking garage application with two browser portals and a small\\nPython CLI:\\n\\n- `/`: attendant control room for check-in, checkout, search, reports, and\\n  upcoming reservations.\\n- `/customer`: guest customer portal for live availability, rate transparency,\\n  near-term reservations, mock payment, lookup, and cancellation.\\n\\nThe core parking logic is framework-independent Python. The current application\\nuses in-memory state; restarting the process resets active cars, reservations,\\nstaff users, sessions, and transaction history.\\n\\n## Features and policies\\n\\n- Configurable levels, spot counts, and rates through `ParkingGarage`.\\n- Compact vehicles prefer compact spots and overflow into standard spots.\\n- Standard vehicles prefer standard spots and overflow into compact spots.\\n- Neither compact nor standard vehicles can use EV spots.\\n- EV vehicles can use only EV spots.\\n- Free spots are indexed by `SpotType`; active cars are indexed by canonical\\n  plate.\\n- Indian plates accept formats such as `KA01AB1234` and `MH-12-CD-5678`.\\n  They are uppercased and stored as `KA-01-AB-1234`.\\n- Fees are displayed in Indian Rupees (`₹`). Values remain numeric `Decimal`\\n  values internally.\\n- Partial hours always round up. A zero-duration or one-minute stay charges at\\n  least the first-hour rate.\\n- The normal `RateCard` daily cap limits one continuous parking stay.\\n- The `/clock` auto-close sweep force-closes active stays over 24 hours. Its\\n  billing uses rolling 24-hour periods from entry: a 30-hour stay is billed as\\n  two daily caps, and a 49-hour stay as three daily caps.\\n\\n## Setup in Codespaces\\n\\nFrom the repository root:\\n\\n```bash\\npython3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt\\npython3 -m pytest -v\\npython3 -m uvicorn src.api:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000\\n```\\n\\nThe alternative launcher is:\\n\\n```bash\\npython3 run.py\\n```\\n\\nOpen port `8000` in the VS Code Codespaces **Ports** panel. The URLs are:\\n\\n- Attendant portal: `http://localhost:8000/`\\n- Staff login: `http://localhost:8000/login`\\n- Customer portal: `http://localhost:8000/customer`\\n\\nThe browser portals poll the backend every seven seconds instead of using\\nWebSockets. This is intentionally simple for the in-memory FastAPI deployment.\\n\\n## Configuration\\n\\nThere are currently no required environment variables. The default application\\nconfiguration is defined in `src/api.py`:\\n\\n- 3 levels\\n- 10 compact spots per level\\n- 15 standard spots per level\\n- 5 EV spots per level\\n- first hour: `50`\\n- additional hour: `30`\\n- daily cap: `200`\\n\\n`src/auth.py` currently uses an in-memory `AuthStore` and a development fallback\\nsigning secret. The secret is not read from an environment variable yet. Do not\\nuse this authentication setup as production security without moving users,\\nsessions, and the signing secret to durable, environment-based configuration.\\n\\n## Portals\\n\\n### Attendant portal\\n\\nThe attendant dashboard provides check-in, checkout, plate lookup, availability,\\nreports, transaction history, an upcoming-reservation queue, and conversion of a\\npaid reservation into an active check-in. It also exposes the staff identity in\\nthe sidebar after login.\\n\\nStaff can create an account and sign in at `/login`. Passwords are stored as\\nPBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hashes. Successful signup/login sets an HTTP-only,\\nSameSite cookie named `staff_session`.\\n\\n### Customer portal\\n\\nThe customer portal is intentionally guest-first. Customers do not need an\\naccount to reserve, pay, find, or cancel a reservation. The current UI supports:\\n\\n- live compact, standard, and EV availability;\\n- the current ₹ rate card;\\n- Indian plate input and a same-day/near-term arrival window;\\n- explicit UPI or cash-at-gate selection;\\n- mock UPI ID validation and confirmation;\\n- reservation confirmation details immediately after payment/confirmation;\\n- lookup by plate or six-character confirmation code;\\n- cancellation before check-in.\\n\\nCustomer email accounts are not implemented. This keeps one-time parking\\nlow-friction, as requested.\\n\\n## Reservation rules\\n\\n- Confirmation codes are six uppercase letters/digits.\\n- A plate can have at most one active pending or paid reservation.\\n- Reservations are limited to the next 24 hours.\\n- A pending UPI reservation does not consume a free spot. The payment window is\\n  10 minutes.\\n- UPI payment holds a compatible spot only after the mock payment succeeds.\\n- Cash confirmation holds a compatible spot and reports `payment_status: pending`;\\n  cash collection is represented by `POST /api/reservations/{code}/cash-collected`.\\n- Paid/cash-held reservations release their spot on cancellation or expiration.\\n- `POST /clock` applies the no-show rule as part of the same sweep as active-car\\n  auto-close: a reservation whose arrival window ended more than 30 minutes ago\\n  is expired and its held spot is released. A checked-in reservation is not\\n  cancelled by this sweep.\\n\\nThe current code also invokes reservation expiry during some ordinary garage\\noperations. For exact grace-period testing, use `/clock`, which is the intended\\nnightly sweep hook and is covered by the tests.\\n\\n## API reference\\n\\n### Pages and static assets\\n\\n- `GET /` - attendant dashboard; redirects to `/login` after at least one staff\\n  account exists and the request has no valid staff cookie.\\n- `GET /login` - staff login page.\\n- `GET /customer` - customer portal; no staff authentication required.\\n- `GET /static/{asset_path}` - CSS and JavaScript assets.\\n\\n### Authentication\\n\\n- `POST /api/auth/signup`\\n  - body: `{\\\"name\\\":\\\"Asha Rao\\\",\\\"email\\\":\\\"asha@example.com\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"securepass\\\"}`\\n- `POST /api/auth/login`\\n  - body: `{\\\"email\\\":\\\"asha@example.com\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"securepass\\\"}`\\n- `POST /api/auth/logout`\\n- `GET /api/auth/me`\\n\\n### Live garage operations\\n\\n- `POST /api/check-in`\\n  - body: `{\\\"plate\\\":\\\"KA01AB1234\\\",\\\"vehicle_type\\\":\\\"ev\\\"}`\\n- `POST /api/check-out`\\n  - body: `{\\\"plate\\\":\\\"KA-01-AB-1234\\\"}`\\n- `GET /api/vehicle/{plate}`\\n- `GET /api/spots/availability`\\n- `GET /api/spots/availability/{compact|standard|ev}`\\n- `GET /api/transactions`\\n  - optional `plate`, `from_date`, `to_date`, `page`, and `page_size` query\\n    parameters.\\n- `GET /api/dashboard`\\n- `GET /api/reports`\\n\\n### Customer and reservations\\n\\n- `GET /api/customer/config` - current rate card and 10-minute payment window.\\n- `POST /api/reservations`\\n  - body includes `plate`, `vehicle_type`, `arrival_start`, `arrival_end`, and\\n    optional `payment_method` (`upi` or `cash`).\\n- `POST /api/reservations/{code}/pay`\\n  - optional body: `{\\\"payment_method\\\":\\\"upi\\\",\\\"upi_id\\\":\\\"name@bank\\\"}`.\\n  - A no-body request remains supported for backward compatibility in the\\n    current test suite.\\n- `GET /api/reservations/lookup?plate=...` or `?code=...`\\n- `POST /api/reservations/{code}/cancel`\\n- `POST /api/reservations/{code}/check-in`\\n- `POST /api/reservations/{code}/cash-collected`\\n- `GET /api/reservations`\\n\\n### Maintenance and valet operations\\n\\n- `POST /clock`\\n  - body is exactly one of `{\\\"set_time\\\":\\\"2026-09-18T14:00:00\\\"}` or\\n    `{\\\"advance_hours\\\":25}`.\\n  - Returns the updated time and tickets auto-closed in that sweep.\\n- `POST /transfer`\\n  - body: `{\\\"old_plate\\\":\\\"KA01AB1234\\\",\\\"new_plate\\\":\\\"MH12CD5678\\\"}`.\\n  - Keeps the same spot and entry time without releasing the spot.\\n\\n## Errors and debugging\\n\\nCommon status codes:\\n\\n- `400`: invalid plate, invalid time/rate input, or another expected domain\\n  validation error.\\n- `401`: invalid staff credentials or unauthenticated `/api/auth/me`.\\n- `404`: missing active vehicle or reservation.\\n- `409`: duplicate active plate, no compatible spot, duplicate reservation,\\n  conflicting reservation state, or occupied transfer destination.\\n- `422`: malformed request validation, invalid clock command, or malformed\\n  lookup/filter input.\\n\\nUseful commands:\\n\\n```bash\\n# Run everything\\npython3 -m pytest -v\\n\\n# Run one layer\\npython3 -m pytest tests/test_rate_card.py -q\\npython3 -m pytest tests/test_garage.py -q\\npython3 -m pytest tests/test_api.py -q\\n\\n# Check syntax\\npython3 -m compileall -q src tests\\n```\\n\\nTo reset all in-memory state, stop and restart Uvicorn. That clears the garage,\\nreservations, staff users, sessions, clock, and history. Tests isolate their\\n`ParkingGarage` instances and monkeypatch the API garage fixture.\\n\\nIf `/` redirects unexpectedly, sign up or log in at `/login`. If a plate is\\nrejected, use two state letters, two RTO digits, one or two series letters, and\\nfour digits, with optional hyphens. If a payment hold is unavailable, check\\n`/api/spots/availability` and the reservation status returned by the API.\\n\\n## CLI\\n\\nThe alternate CLI remains in `src/cli.py`:\\n\\n```bash\\npython3 -m src.cli\\n```\\n\\nIt supports check-in, checkout, availability, active-car lookup, and exit. It is\\nseparate from both browser portals and is retained as a useful development and\\noperations interface.\\n\\n## Rate-card import status\\n\\nNo messy rate-card payload was present in the project or supplied specification;\\nthe earlier placeholder was literally `<PASTE YOUR MESSY RATE CARD DATA HERE>`.\\nTherefore no T4 cleaning module was invented and no production rates were\\nsilently changed. The active app still constructs `RateCard(50, 30, 200)` in\\n`build_garage()`. A real importer should be added only after the actual source\\npayload is supplied.\\n\\n## Known limitations and next steps\\n\\n- State is process-local and disappears on restart; add a database and durable\\n  migrations for production.\\n- Staff users and sessions are in memory; move them to durable storage and read\\n  the signing secret from an environment variable.\\n- Most operational API routes remain callable without a staff cookie for\\n  backward compatibility; only the attendant HTML root is redirect-gated when\\n  accounts exist.\\n- Mock UPI and cash collection have no real payment provider or audit ledger.\\n- The CLI does not include reservations or staff authentication.\\n- Polling is used instead of WebSockets.\\n- The rate-card importer is still pending the real dirty input data.\\n- Add persistent reservations, role-based staff permissions, CSRF protection,\\n  rate-card versioning, and structured audit logging next.\\n\"}"

                  "name": "create_file",
                  "arguments": "{\"filePath\":\"/workspaces/Parking_Garage/REASONING.md\",\"content\":\"# Implementation Reasoning\\n\\nThis document describes the system that is actually in the repository, not an\\nintended future architecture.\\n\\n## Core design\\n\\n### `Vehicle`\\n\\n`Vehicle` owns the license plate and `SpotType`. Construction calls\\n`normalize_plate`, so all domain objects use one canonical Indian plate form:\\n`STATE-RTO-SERIES-NUMBER`, such as `KA-01-AB-1234`.\\n\\n### `Spot`\\n\\n`Spot` represents one physical location with a level, spot type, charger flag,\\nand occupancy metadata. EV spots are created with `has_charger=True`. The\\n`reservation_code`, `vehicle`, and `ticket_id` references make the current\\nphysical state visible without searching history.\\n\\n### `Ticket`\\n\\n`Ticket` is the live or completed parking session. It records the vehicle,\\nspot, entry/exit timestamps, fee, generated ticket ID, and whether the session\\nwas force-closed by the 24-hour sweep.\\n\\n### `RateCard`\\n\\n`RateCard` is isolated from garage allocation. It accepts already-clean numeric\\nrates and calculates a per-stay fee using `Decimal`. It rounds a partial hour\\nup and charges at least one first-hour rate, including for an immediate\\ncheckout. Normal fees are capped by `daily_cap`.\\n\\n### `Clock`\\n\\n`Clock` is a small thread-safe injectable time source. It defaults to\\n`datetime.now()` but supports `set_time` and `advance_hours`, allowing tests\\nand `POST /clock` to exercise time-dependent behavior without waiting.\\n\\n### `Reservation`\\n\\n`Reservation` records a six-character confirmation code, canonical plate,\\nvehicle type, arrival window, payment deadline, status, held spot, payment\\nmethod, payment status, and displayed payment amount. `PaymentMethod` supports\\nUPI and cash; `PaymentStatus` distinguishes pending, paid, and collected.\\n\\n### `ParkingGarage`\\n\\n`ParkingGarage` owns spot construction and the state transitions for check-in,\\ncheckout, reservations, auto-close, and transfer. A single `Lock` protects\\nallocation, releases, reservations, transfer, and history mutations.\\n\\n## O(1)-style live lookups\\n\\nThe garage deliberately separates live state from completed history:\\n\\n- `active_tickets: dict[str, Ticket]` maps canonical plate to the current car.\\n- `free_spots: dict[SpotType, set[str]]` tracks available physical spot IDs.\\n- `spots: dict[str, Spot]` resolves a spot ID to its level and state.\\n- `reservations: dict[str, Reservation]` indexes confirmation codes.\\n- `reservation_by_plate: dict[str, str]` enforces one active reservation per\\n  plate and supports plate lookup without scanning the log.\\n- `history: list[Ticket]` is append-only completed transaction history.\\n\\nCheck-in pops from a compatible free set; checkout returns the spot to that\\nset. Plate lookup, free-spot checks, and active-state checks do not scan\\n`history`, so historical growth does not make those operations linear in the\\nday's transaction count. Reservation lookup by plate is an index lookup; the\\nhistory list is not involved.\\n\\n## T4 messy rate-card import\\n\\nT4 is not implemented. The supplied material contained the literal placeholder\\n`<PASTE YOUR MESSY RATE CARD DATA HERE>`, not actual rows. Consequently:\\n\\n- there is no `clean_rate_card` importer module;\\n- no duplicate-row or missing-field tie-break rule was applied;\\n- no broken-row behavior can honestly be documented;\\n- `build_garage()` still constructs `RateCard(50, 30, 200)`.\\n\\nInventing a cleaning rule or rates without source data would silently alter\\nbilling. The correct next step is to add a separate parser with explicit tests\\nonce the real payload is available. `RateCard` already receives clean values\\nand remains independent of parsing.\\n\\n## T2 rolling-24-hour billing and `/clock`\\n\\n`ParkingGarage.auto_close_overdue()` runs under the same lock as normal\\ncheckout. It scans active tickets only, identifies sessions strictly over 24\\nhours, removes them from `active_tickets`, computes:\\n\\n```text\\nceil((clock_time - entry_time) / 24 hours) * daily_cap\\n```\\n\\nand releases the spot. The ticket is appended to history with\\n`auto_closed=True`. A normal checkout removes the ticket first, so a later\\nsweep cannot process it twice.\\n\\n`POST /clock` updates the shared `Clock`, runs the reservation no-show sweep,\\nthen runs active-session auto-close, and returns the auto-closed tickets. It is\\nthe test hook standing in for a nightly cron job.\\n\\nThe clock endpoint accepts either `set_time` or `advance_hours`, but not both.\\nThe default garage and API clock are process-local, so restarting the server\\nresets the simulated time and all other state.\\n\\n## T6 valet transfer\\n\\n`ParkingGarage.transfer(old_plate, new_plate)` normalizes both plates and runs\\nunder the garage lock. It verifies that the old plate is active and the new\\nplate is not. It then changes the ticket's plate and vehicle reference and\\nupdates the occupied spot's vehicle reference. It never removes or re-adds the\\nspot in `free_spots`, so availability cannot flicker to free during transfer.\\nEntry time, spot ID, ticket ID, and subsequent fee calculation remain intact.\\nThe API maps missing sessions to 404 and an occupied destination to 409.\\n\\n## Reservation holds and no-show behavior\\n\\nThe intended reservation lifecycle is:\\n\\n1. Create a near-term reservation. A normal UPI reservation starts as\\n   `pending_payment` and does not remove a spot from `free_spots`.\\n2. Confirm UPI payment. The backend atomically pops a compatible spot and marks\\n   the reservation paid.\\n3. Confirm cash-at-gate. The current payment endpoint can switch the\\n   reservation to cash and hold a compatible spot immediately; its payment\\n   status remains pending until the cash-collection endpoint is called.\\n4. Cancel, check in, or expire the reservation. Cancellation and expiration\\n   release a held spot; conversion changes the reserved spot into an occupied\\n   active ticket.\\n\\nThe shared `/clock` sweep applies the 30-minute no-show grace rule to paid\\nreservations: after an arrival window has ended by more than 30 minutes, the\\nreservation is expired and its held spot is released. Checked-in reservations\\nhave status `checked_in` and are not touched. Keeping this in the same sweep\\nas T2 ensures one simulated nightly event updates both overdue cars and\\nno-show reservations atomically under the garage lock.\\n\\nImportant current-state detail: ordinary reservation reads and some garage\\noperations call the general expiry helper without the grace flag, while\\n`auto_close_overdue()` calls it with `apply_no_show_grace=True`. The documented\\nand tested grace-period mechanism is therefore specifically the `/clock`\\nsweep; this is an area to simplify if the expiry semantics are hardened later.\\n\\n## Authentication design\\n\\n`AuthStore` is an in-memory staff identity/session service:\\n\\n- staff signup accepts name, email, and an eight-character minimum password;\\n- passwords are PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hashes with per-user salts;\\n- login issues a signed, HTTP-only, SameSite cookie;\\n- logout removes the server-side session mapping;\\n- the attendant root redirects to `/login` after at least one account exists;\\n- `/api/auth/me` supplies the sidebar identity.\\n\\nCustomers deliberately remain guest users. A plate plus confirmation code is\\nsufficient for reservation lookup/cancellation, which avoids account friction\\nfor a one-time parking visit. Optional customer email accounts are not built.\\n\\nThis is suitable for a demonstrator, not production authentication. The store\\nand sessions are process-local, the fallback signing secret is in code, and\\nmost operational API routes are not protected by an auth dependency yet. A\\nproduction version should use a database, an environment secret, expiration,\\nCSRF protection, and route-level authorization.\\n\\n## Known limitations and next steps\\n\\n- T4 rate-card import is blocked on missing source data.\\n- No persistent database exists.\\n- No real UPI gateway or payment ledger exists.\\n- Cash collection is a state transition, not a financial reconciliation flow.\\n- Polling is used instead of WebSockets.\\n- The CLI supports core parking operations but not reservations or auth.\\n- Reports use process-local history and `datetime.now()` rather than a durable\\n  reporting clock.\\n- Add durable storage, migrations, role-based staff permissions, route-level\\n  auth dependencies, environment configuration, structured audit events, and\\n  integration/browser tests next.\\n\"}"
